findings.title: Claims F21 is not fixed: the page's new explanation for the 26 vs 27 gap is wrong, and the example is not 'the same shape'
findings.location: build-comparison/src/app.html:1509 (writeResults, example sentence) and :1421 exampleSheet()
findings.evidence:
The page now says: "The example is the median soldier at 1.80 m ... The limits section reads the same shape at 27 from a larger drawing; the reading moves by a few percent with the drawing's size." exampleSheet() still draws e.girths, his own girths at 1.755 m, on a 1.80 m frame. compute_limits.js uses calc.compute({heightM: 1.8}), his shape scaled to 1.80 m. Script scratchpad/review2/s/f21.js, page settings (1,060 kg/m³, 7.5% fat):
- page example, own girths, 700 px, default refine: 25.70 (90.0 kg)
- own girths at 800 px: 25.82
- own girths at 1,600 px: 25.82
- girths at 1.80 m, 800 px: 27.26, which is limits.json score_at_f1
A larger drawing changes the reading by 0.5%. The girth basis changes it by (1.8/1.755)² = 5.2%. The round 1 verifier gave this cause and fix (round1.json, claims F21 better_fix). HEAD kept the explanation the verifier had shown to be wrong. round1.md says all 23 confirmed claims findings were fixed.
findings.expected: The tool example and the limits card read one stated shape and give one number. Otherwise the page gives the true cause of the difference.
findings.fix: In exampleSheet(), take girths at 1.80 m as drawTarget does: var r0 = calc.compute({ buildId: 'ansur2_m_p50', heightM: 1.8 }); BuildCalc.SITES.forEach(function (s) { g[s] = r0.girths[s].value; }). Then delete the sentence 'The limits section reads the same shape at ... with the drawing's size.' The example then measures about 27, the same as the card.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced on HEAD 1f32e2c. The only commits after 7061d55 touch STATUS.md and history/, so build-comparison is unchanged and the working tree is clean. In Chromium the tool example shows 'Mass 90 kg', 'Score 26 (24–28)' and the sentence: 'The limits section reads the same shape at 27 from a larger drawing; the reading moves by a few percent with the drawing's size.' The limits card shows 27 for 'The median soldier's own shape'.

exampleSheet() (app.html:1421-1427) draws e.girths, his own girths at 1.755 m, on a 1.80 m frame. compute_limits.js maker() uses calc.compute({heightM: 1.8}), whose girths are 1.8/1.755 = 1.0256 times larger. My Node run (fixv/s/f21.js) uses the page's own options (top reference, default refine):
- own girths: 25.70 at 700 px, 25.70 at 800 px, 25.76 at 1,600 px. Drawing size moves the reading by 0.2%.
- girths at 1.80 m: 26.86 at 700 px, 27.13 at 800 px.
- limits.json score_at_f1 is 27.26.
The girth basis accounts for about 5% of the gap and the drawing size for under 1%. The page's explanation is wrong. Its example is also not 'the same shape' as the card, and not 'the median soldier at 1.80 m' in the same-shape sense: it is a slimmer body. The round 1 verifier gave this exact cause and fix, and HEAD kept the wrong sentence.

findings.title: UX L8 is only half fixed: tapping the 924 ring at its centre or anywhere on its left half still jumps to 'Empty to the end'
findings.location: build-comparison/src/app.html:1218 stopAt (now d <= best.d) and :1727 tapeJump; research/reviews/round1.md:83
findings.evidence: Script scratchpad/review2/s/l8.js taps the circle.m924 ring at offsets from its centre and records the id that jump() scrolls to. At 1280 px and 390 px (touch), on both the glance tape (ring 14 px) and the locator (ring 7 px): -6, -4, -2, -1 and 0 px go to 'empty-3'; +1 to +4 px go to 'meatball'. The round 1 verifier predicted this (round1.json L8): 'Changing to d <= best.d alone does not fix it: a tap a hair left of the ring centre still has gap d=0 and meatball d>0.' Its fix, a snap in tapeJump, was not applied. round1.md:83 says 'L8: the 924 ring jumps to the meatball.'
findings.expected: A tap anywhere on the ring, which marks the meatball, jumps to the meatball stop.
findings.fix: In tapeJump, before stopAt: if (Math.abs(x - X(MEAT)) <= 8) { jump('meatball'); return; }. Here x is the tap position in the host and X = host._X. Add the dx = -3 tap to shots.js.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced with my own script (fixv/s/l8.js), which dispatches clicks at offsets from X(MEAT) on #glance and #locTape at 1280 px and at 390 px (touch). The results are the same on both tapes and at both widths: dx = -6, -4, -2, -1, -0.5, 0 and +0.5 go to 'empty-3'; +1, +2, +4 and +6 go to 'meatball'. A real mouse click at the ring centre at 1280 px (s/l8real.js) scrolls to 'Empty to the end', and the locator then reads 'now: empty 220 to 924'.

The cause is in stopAt. The last gap's hi equals MEAT (924.099), so any score below MEAT has gap d = 0 and meatball d > 0. The change to d <= best.d only fixes ties at or above MEAT. So tapping the centre or the left half of the ring, which marks the meatball, still lands on the gap, and round1.md:83 ('L8: the 924 ring jumps to the meatball') is only half true. One small error in the finding: the locator's ring radius is 3.5 px, not 7.

findings.title: UX L1 is partly fixed: on the pressed segmented buttons the inside focus ring is 2.3:1 (light) and 1.7:1 (dark) against the button
findings.location: build-comparison/src/app.html:58 (.seg button:focus-visible { outline-offset: -4px }); research/reviews/round1.md:76
findings.evidence:
Script scratchpad/review2/s/focus3.js focuses each segmented button with focusVisible. The ring now sits inside the button, so the button's fill is on both sides of it.
- Light, pressed hSame/vFront/zAll: ring rgb(31,79,166) on rgb(21,24,31), contrast 2.31:1
- Dark, pressed: ring rgb(148,181,255) on rgb(232,233,238), contrast 1.68:1. Screenshot scratchpad/review2/shots/f-hSame-dark.png shows a faint pale-blue ring.
The unpressed buttons are fine (7.3 and 8.3:1). The pressed buttons are the defaults (Same height, Front, Whole scale), so a keyboard user meets these first. The round 1 verifier's fix included 'a sheet-coloured inner ring so it also shows on the pressed (ink) button'. That part was not applied, and round1.md does not say so.
findings.expected: A focus indicator of at least 3:1 against the colours next to it (WCAG 1.4.11) on every segmented button, pressed or not.
findings.fix: Add: .seg button[aria-pressed="true"]:focus-visible { outline-color: var(--sheet); }. The sheet colour on the pressed fill gives 16.7:1 (light) and 13.9:1 (dark). Alternatively use the verifier's box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 4px var(--sheet).

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced (fixv/s/focus.js, screenshots fixv/shots/f-*.png). With focus({focusVisible: true}), each pressed segmented button (hSame, vFront, zAll, the defaults) has outline-offset -4px. The ring lies on the button's own fill:
- light: ring rgb(31,79,166) on rgb(21,24,31), 2.31:1
- dark: ring rgb(148,181,255) on rgb(232,233,238), 1.68:1
The unpressed buttons give 7.26:1 (light) and 8.27:1 (dark) against the effective background.

The ring is visible but faint on the pressed buttons, below the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks for focus indicators. The round 1 verifier's 'sheet-coloured inner ring' was not applied, and round1.md:76 records L1 as fixed without saying so.

findings.title: Claims F6 is partly fixed: the key still defines ESTIMATE as 'body fat assumed', but Brian Shaw's ESTIMATE rests on a reported body fat
findings.location: build-comparison/src/app.html:1698 (key: 'ESTIMATE: body fat assumed. DERIVED: body fat measured.') and :439 (forest sub: 'Every range is an estimate (body fat assumed) unless ...')
findings.evidence: scoreStatus now returns 'estimate' unless bodyFat.status is 'measured', so Brian Shaw's plate and forest row read ESTIMATE. His drawer shows 'BODY FAT 18% (15–21%) REPORTED The build's own measured or reported value' (scratchpad/review2/drawers.json). He is the only build with bodyFat.status 'reported' (node check over model.all()). The key and the forest sub explain his chip as 'body fat assumed', which his own drawer contradicts. The round 1 verifier's better_fix was to reword both texts to 'ESTIMATE: body fat assumed or only reported'. They were not changed.
findings.expected: The key's meaning for each chip matches every build that carries it.
findings.fix: Key: 'ESTIMATE: body fat assumed or only reported. DERIVED: body fat measured in a study.' Forest sub: '... an estimate (body fat assumed or only reported) unless it carries a DERIVED chip (body fat measured)'.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced. The page's key text reads 'How sure the score is. ESTIMATE: body fat assumed. DERIVED: body fat measured.' The forest sub reads 'Every range is an estimate (body fat assumed) unless it carries a DERIVED chip (body fat measured).'

Brian Shaw's plate chip is ESTIMATE, from scoreStatus: bodyFat.status !== 'measured'. His drawer says 'BODY FAT 18% (15–21%) REPORTED The build's own measured or reported value'. A tally over model.all() finds he is the only build with bodyFat.status 'reported'; every other ESTIMATE has 'estimate' body fat. So the key's definition is false for him, and the round 1 verifier's rewording was not applied.
verdict.better_fix: app.html:1698 key: 'ESTIMATE: body fat assumed or only reported. DERIVED: body fat measured in a study.' app.html:439 forest sub: '… an estimate (body fat assumed or only reported) unless it carries a DERIVED chip (body fat measured in a study).'

findings.title: round1.md overstates the per-view refinement speed-up ('about a third faster')
findings.location: build-comparison/research/reviews/round1.md:100 (code F5 row)
findings.evidence:
Scripts scratchpad/review2/s/prof.js and s/refine_browser.js compare measure.js at 3cd65f5 (whole-sheet refinement) with HEAD (refineViews). The input is the 2,000 px median-soldier sheet, 4,479 × 2,320 px, made with templateViews and renderSheet.
- Node, refinement only: 8,866 and 8,244 ms (old) against 7,091 and 7,115 ms (new), 14–20% faster
- Node, full measureSheet: 10,723 and 10,014 ms against 8,819 and 8,986 ms
- Chromium, full measureSheet: 11,481 and 10,737 ms against 9,611 and 10,698 ms (0–16%)
The masks are identical (0 pixels differ) and so is the score (26.95). The worker and 'about 10 s' parts of the row are true: 10.1 s in the page, with a largest timer gap of 171 ms while it runs.
findings.expected: The review record gives the speed-up it measured.
findings.fix: Change 'about a third faster' to 'about 10–20% faster (refinement 8.2–8.9 s down to 7.1 s on a 2,000 px sheet)'. Alternatively, make it faster, for example by refining only a band a few pixels wide around the coarse mask edge.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced in Node (fixv/s/prof.js, s/prof2.js). I compared measure.js before the change (7b6306e~1, whole-sheet refinement) with HEAD (refineViews). The input is the 2,000 px median-soldier sheet, 4,479 × 2,320 px, from templateViews and renderSheet, measured with the page's options.

Full measureSheet, warm, alternating:
- new: 9,666, 8,841 and 9,149 ms
- old: 10,804, 10,827 and 10,405 ms
- 10–18% faster

Refinement alone (subtracting the refine:0 runs of about 1.6 s): about 7.2–8.3 s against 8.8–9.2 s, 12–22% faster. The masks are identical (0 pixels differ) and so is the score (26.953).

'About a third faster' (round1.md:100) overstates it. It probably compares against the verifier's 16 s, which was inflated by other jobs running at the same time. The '~10 s' and worker parts of the row are accurate.
verdict.better_fix: round1.md:100: 'Refinement runs on each view's crop: 10–20% faster on a 2,000 px sheet (about 10.5 s down to 9 s in Node), and much less memory.' Or make it a real speed-up by refining only a band about 2 × refineDist px around the coarse mask edge.

findings.title: round1.md says each archive.org API source now shows its quote and its book's page; 4 of 21 show neither, including the official 1987 handbook hit

findings.evidence: A Python check over data/facts.json found 21 page_production sources, 4 with no 'it matched' quote. All 4 are in asgardian_tissue_density_ohotmu ('OHOTMU 1987 TPB vol 4: same phrases'; 'times the density' AND Asgardian; 'dense/denser/density') and asgardian_tissue_density_dk. research/archive_snippets.json stores a hit for the 1987 handbook (officialhandbook04grue, an official item): '... bone is about 3 times {{{denser than similar human tissue}}}, contributing to the Asgardians ...'. Reproduced in Chromium (scratchpad/review2v/c2/br.js race).

**Steps:**
1. Load big-p95.png (4,490 × 2,320, a 2,000 px figure), type 1.80 and press Measure.
2. 0.3 s later, load small-wide.png (1,022 × 522).

| The page's (unscaled) | 25.83 | 25.82 |

findings.title: Two quick measurements: two elapsed-time counters overwrite each other, and the new job waits behind the abandoned one
findings.location: src/app.html measureAsync() (a new setInterval per call) and the tSoldier handler (calls measure() while the button is disabled)

findings.title: Tests do not cover what the round-1 fixes claim: no test sees the worker path, and an arms-flag assertion cannot fail
findings.location: test/shots.js (tool waits); test/test.js "the chart's own figures …" and "each headline limit's score …"
findings.evidence:
- **Worker.** shots.js waits only for results rows and the duo.jpg validation. With a worker script that throws on load, or Worker undefined, the page falls back to the main thread and shows the same score, "Score 26 (24–28)" (code/fallback.js). A broken worker therefore passes CI, although the F5 fix is 'measuring runs in a Web Worker'.
- **Arms flag.** `assert.strictEqual(c.arms, c.rest_deg >= L.arms.angle_deg)` compares the fresh run's flag with the fresh run's own rest angle. compute_limits defines arms as exactly rest >= angle, so this can fail only through the 0.1° rounding of rest_deg.
- **Thighs and face flags** are never checked against Fig.thighContact or Fig.elbowFlexion.
- **Face limit.** The 'headline limit … tool's reading' test re-measures only arms and thighs, so the face reading (arms at 92°, not found; see C2-1) is untested.
findings.expected: Each test should be able to fail on the defect its name describes.
findings.fix:
- In shots.js, record Worker construction and a message from it with an init script, and fail if the tool fell back.
- Recompute the thighs and face flags from the figure in the test.
- Add the face item to the re-measure test, with an assertion that the arms were found.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced, with one part softened.

**Worker.** test/shots.js never mentions Worker. In Chromium I ran the page twice: once with `window.Worker = undefined`, once with a Worker whose script throws on load. Both show the same "Score 26 (24–28)" and log no console error, because worker.onerror calls preventDefault and falls back to the page. So a broken worker passes CI, although round1.md code F5 says measuring now runs in a Web Worker.

**Flags (mutation test).** In a copy I changed compute_limits.js so the face flag is `elbowFlexion < 140` (30 chart builds then 'meet' the face test, Captain America among them) and the thighs flag is `thighContact >= 0.3`. I regenerated limits.json and ran node test/test.js: "30 passed, 0 failed". The test named "…the tests match the stored flags" checks only the arms flag.

**Softened part.** The claim that the arms-flag assertion 'cannot fail' is too strong. limitsRun is the fresh run, but rest_deg is independently re-derived (`near(Fig.armRestAngle(mk), c.rest_deg, 0.1)`), so the assertion does pin the arms definition and threshold.

**Face re-measure.** The 'headline limit' test leaves out the face limit. Its name covers only headline limits, and face has headline: false, so that part is a coverage gap rather than a mislabelled test.
